summary.headline: FY26 total income rose 14.15% to INR115.58 crore and net profit 31.04% to INR8.11 crore; FY27 turnover target INR200 crore (40-45% growth).
summary.overview: Gabion Technologies reported FY26 total income of INR115.58 crore (+14.15% YoY), EBITDA of INR17.79 crore (+15.75%) and net profit of INR8.11 crore (+31.04%). H2 FY26 was stronger: total income INR74.87 crore (+29.44%), EBITDA INR11.91 crore (+72.09%, margin 15.91%) and net profit INR5.69 crore (+62.53%). Management said FY26 growth fell short of the 20-25% earlier guided, citing about INR15 crore of near-complete project work not built in the year. The current order book is about INR200 crore, split 50% products and 50% projects, and management targets FY27 turnover of INR200 crore, with FY28 above INR300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Management expects similar level in FY27

segments.name: Products (manufacturing, external sales)
segments.commentary: About 46-50% of FY26 revenue (around INR50-53 crore); FY26 output about 8,000 tonnes valued at about INR75 crore, of which about INR25 crore was consumed internally. Product margin about 10 percentage points below services.

segments.name: Projects / Services (EPC, installation)
segments.commentary: About INR54 crore in FY26 (about 50% of revenue); the main growth driver in FY26. Margin about 10 percentage points above products; management expects project margin to rise 1-2 points in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover target of INR200 crore, about 40-45% growth over FY26, driven by product capacity doubling and project turnover.

Production capacity to reach 18,000 tonnes by September 2026 (from about 12,000 tonnes now, 15,000 after current machinery), translating to about INR180-200 crore of product sales at full utilisation.
FY28 turnover expected above INR300 crore, per management's earlier comment.
Operating margin expected to rise 1-2 percentage points in FY27 on economies of scale and higher-margin mix; management also cited 0.1-2% improvement.
Finance cost expected to stay around INR4.7 crore in FY27.
Around 90% of the current order book expected to be executed in FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR4 crore, funded by internal accruals and bank loan; a further INR2 crore ongoing (machinery on the way, buildings under construction).
Total capex since last year about INR8 crore; about INR1 crore of the remainder funded from IPO proceeds for a final machinery batch, pending technical due diligence.
Capacity path: 9,000 tonnes last year, 12,000 tonnes currently, 15,000 tonnes after pending machinery, 18,000 tonnes by September 2026.
New factory in Assam; facilities in 29 states and a manufacturing unit in Nepal.
Capacity utilisation about 80%, with more than 170 machines; management said demand exceeds capacity and export opportunities are in the pipeline but capacity-constrained.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crore, including products (government and private buyers) and existing customers; INR44 crore booked so far in FY27 (as of May).
Of the order book, about 50% is ongoing projects started mid-FY26 and about INR50 crore is newly started or about to start projects.

Management claims about 20-25% market share in gabions; named competitors are Secure Matrix (Maharashtra), Techfire and smaller players. SRM Contractors is a major customer, though also a competitor in projects.
Steel and polymer price risk: management books large orders with suppliers and says it can renegotiate prices, citing force majeure clauses; polymer prices roughly doubled during the Iran war.
Product execution takes about one month typically (up to 3-4 months for large orders); project execution takes 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 growth about 14% against the 20-25% guided at the IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about INR15 crore of project work nearly complete on site but not built during the year; it is excluded from the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200 crore order book fully executable in FY27 and does it include products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book is about 50% products and 50% projects, is all to be executed in FY27 and includes product orders.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why do inventory and receivables look elevated against a 45-60 day cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the inventory rise to about INR15 crore of unbilled project work-in-progress and said receivables rose because of about INR50 crore of sales in the last quarter; it expects receivables around INR40 crore going forward, with working capital not rising in FY27 despite sales nearly doubling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gap between product and service margins, and what drove FY26 margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Services margin is about 10 points above manufacturing (roughly 20% vs 10%); FY26 margin expansion was driven by the higher service mix (about 45%).

qa_highlights.question: How will steel and polymer price increases affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it books large orders with suppliers (up to three months' cover) and can renegotiate product prices; it did not give a margin figure at current raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex about INR8 crore since last year, with about INR1 crore from IPO proceeds; capacity to reach 18,000 tonnes by September 2026.

risks_watch: Execution slippage: about INR15 crore of project revenue was deferred into FY27 and cannot yet be recognised, which depends on customer measurement and certification.

Working capital: inventory rose from about INR13 crore to INR35 crore and receivables from INR21 crore to INR43 crore since FY24 (per analyst's figures); management has not reconciled the gap versus the stated 45-60 day product cycle.
Raw material exposure: steel and polymer price spikes; management relies on pre-booked supply and renegotiation, which it cannot fully guarantee for the INR200 crore order book.
Capacity ramp: 18,000 tonnes by September 2026 depends on delivery and installation of the IPO-funded machinery; monsoon slowdown expected from around September to October.
Payment delays from private customers on the 45-day MSME norm, which management says is not uniformly honoured.
FY26 tax treatment: no tax charged in H1 and full-year tax booked in H2 per auditor treatment; this affects quarterly comparability.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, capacity and order visibility, with clear targets (INR200 crore FY27, INR300 crore FY28). Less precise on working capital, raw material pass-through and margin mechanics, where answers were general and some figures were revised during the call.
key_quotes: We are targeting a turnover of INR200 crores in FY27, which will translate into a growth of approximately 40%-45% over FY26 figures.
There is a work in progress in our project amounting to approximately INR15 crores, which could not get built during the financial year.
Our current order book stood at approximately INR200 crores, which provides strong revenue visibility for the coming period and reflects continued customer confidence and deep business momentum.
The margin in services is approximately 10% higher than just in the manufacturing field.

adds.what: Production capacity 12,000 t to 15,000 t after pending machinery batch (3,000 t machinery on the way)
Production capacity to 18,000 t by September 2026
New factory in Assam (buildings under construction)

growth.why: Management targets FY27 turnover of INR200 crore (+40-45%) backed by a INR200 crore order book (INR44 crore booked so far in FY27), capacity rising from 12,000 t to 18,000 t by September 2026, and 80% utilisation; FY28 above INR300 crore, though the 18,000 t path and FY27 EBITDA margin gain of 1-2 pp are not yet fully evidenced with dated contracts.
